newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen maintaining flat trend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen maintaining flat trend.

text.p: Polish shares fell after Friday's gain but analysts said the market should maintain its month-long sideways trend after one more fall on Tuesday signalled by the session's stronger selling after price-fixing.
Analysts said losses by some large-cap stocks on Monday could represent large investors shuffling portfolios before year-end and that steeper falls were not likely.
"Most stocks could fall tomorrow but some heavyweights should rise and the market should continue its horizontal trend," said Jan Koch, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.
Large-cap banks BPH, WBK and BIG fell 4.9 percent, 3.3 percent and 2.6 percent respectively in active trade with only WBK showing stronger selling after price-fixing.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell on percent to 13,653.3 points and turnover rose 16.2 percent to 90 million zlotys ($31.6 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 44 to 30 with nine stocks flat.

Analysts said top gainer trader Universal rose 6.3 percent in moderate trade on Friday's news the firm saw group net profit rising to 60 million zlotys ($21.1 million) in 1997 from its prediction of 47 million zlotys ($16.5 million) for 1996.
Continuous trade turnover was at 3.1 million zlotys ($1.1 million) with four stocks down, two up and three flat.

Mass privatisation NFI units fell two percent to 145 zlotys ($50.9) in a 19.5-million-zloty ($6.8 million) turnover in the regular bourse sesssion and fell 3.4 percent to 142 zlotys ($49.9) in 19.1-million-zloty ($6.7 million) continuous trade.
